findings.source_quote: Μικρὸν ἔχω ἀκαιρεθῆναι, καὶ πάντα σοι ἐπιλύσω
findings.english_quote: I must be occupied elsewhere for a little while, then I will explain everything to you.
findings.issue: “Elsewhere” adds a location not expressed by the selected Greek. The surrounding departure does not make that location part of this clause.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed wording for fresh review: “I must be occupied for a little while, and I will explain everything to you.” Adjust the corresponding description in note d as well.

findings.english_quote: The draft also retains the version-supported working reading about being occupied elsewhere rather than silently treating the reported Athos form as identical.
findings.issue: The note announces an Athos alternative without identifying its wording or meaning. Readers therefore cannot assess the stated distinction. The supplied bounded report does not provide the relevant apparatus entry for this clause.
findings.suggested_revision: Supply an attributed apparatus transcription or bounded comparison report identifying the reported Athos form, and disclose its English alternative or explain why its meaning remains uncertain. Retain the selected working reading pending that clarification; do not imply fresh manuscript verification.

findings.source_quote: ἐγὼ δὲ ἤμην μόνος μετὰ τῶν παρθένων· ἦσαν δὲ ἱλαρώτεραι, καὶ πρὸς ἐμὲ εὖ εἶχον· μάλιστα δὲ αἱ τέσσαρες αἱ ἐνδοξότεραι αὐτῶν.
findings.english_quote: Retain the narrated affection, sibling distinction, the Son’s role and the stated gate/name and clothing requirements.
findings.issue: The per-unit theological metadata attributes sibling distinctions, the Son’s role, and gate/name and clothing requirements to this selected unit, which contains none of those assertions. This obscures which theological decisions actually belong to the reviewed source.
findings.suggested_revision: Replace the copied cross-unit decision with metadata specific to section x, or explicitly label and relocate the broader discussion as cross-unit context rather than a decision about assertions preserved here.

findings.source_quote: ἐπλήρωσε οὖν τοὺς τύπους τῶν λίθων τῶν εἰς τὴν οἰκοδομὴν ἀπεληλυθότων
findings.english_quote: He filled the hollows where the stones had been.
findings.issue: The simplified sentence omits the repeated identification of these stones as having gone into the building. That information occurs earlier, but the selected source explicitly repeats it here.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed wording for fresh review: “He filled the hollows left by the stones that had gone into the building.”

findings.source_quote: Μικρὸν ἔχω ἀκαιρεθῆναι, καὶ πάντα σοι ἐπιλύσω
findings.english_quote: I must be busy elsewhere for a little while. Then I will explain everything.
findings.issue: “Elsewhere” adds a location absent from the selected clause. The simplification also drops the explicit recipient “to you” from the promised explanation.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed wording for fresh review: “I must be busy for a little while. Then I will explain everything to you.” Adjust note d’s description accordingly.

findings.english_quote: The draft also retains the version-supported working reading about being occupied elsewhere rather than silently treating the reported Athos form as identical.
findings.issue: The note mentions a different reported Athos form but supplies neither that form nor its English meaning. The supplied evidence does not contain the relevant apparatus entry, so the claimed distinction is not adequately disclosed.
findings.suggested_revision: Provide an attributed transcription or bounded report for the relevant apparatus entry and state the reported alternative in English, or identify the uncertainty explicitly. Keep the selected working reading rather than substituting an unestablished alternative.

findings.source_quote: ἐγὼ δὲ ἤμην μόνος μετὰ τῶν παρθένων· ἦσαν δὲ ἱλαρώτεραι, καὶ πρὸς ἐμὲ εὖ εἶχον· μάλιστα δὲ αἱ τέσσαρες αἱ ἐνδοξότεραι αὐτῶν.
findings.english_quote: Retain the narrated affection, sibling distinction, the Son’s role and the stated gate/name and clothing requirements.
findings.issue: The theological metadata presents several assertions from outside section x as decisions concerning this unit. The selected source contains friendliness but no sibling distinction, Son identification, or gate/name and clothing requirements.
findings.suggested_revision: Use unit-specific theological metadata, or clearly separate and label any cross-unit contextual discussion.

findings.source_quote: αἱ γὰρ παρθένοι αὗται μετὰ σοῦ εἰσί.
findings.english_quote: Retain ancient repair materials, sibling relationship and affection, gate/name requirements, holy-spirits plural and clothing imagery; preserve all substantive alternative notes.
findings.issue: The simplification metadata claims preservation of a sibling relationship, gate/name requirements, a holy-spirits plural, and clothing imagery that do not occur in this selected source. It therefore misstates what this unit’s simplification preserves.
findings.suggested_revision: Replace this with a description of the actual section-x simplification decisions, retaining only source features present here.

summary: Both editions substantially preserve the selected narrative, its speakers, negations, and necessity. Revisions are needed for an added location, incomplete disclosure of a reported alternative, and cross-unit metadata. The simplified edition also omits explicit repeated information. The bracketed first “everything” is disclosed as an editorial insertion, not silently presented as preserved witness text. This review evaluates the supplied Greek and attributed reports; it does not authenticate unseen manuscripts or certify exhaustive collation. All proposed wording requires fresh review.
